# Per-package statement coverage floors, enforced by tools/coveragefloor
# (wired into .gitlab-ci.yml's `fast` job and .github/workflows/ci.yml's
# `Test` step, right after `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...`).
#
# This is a RATCHET, not a target: a floor here is never lowered to make
# a change pass. If a change legitimately drops a package's coverage
# (e.g. an intentional untested escape hatch), the fix is to add the
# missing test, not to edit this file down. The file is reviewed like any
# other source change -- a pull/merge request that lowers a number here
# should say why in its description.
#
# To RAISE a floor (coverage has genuinely improved and you want to lock
# the gain in so it cannot quietly regress): rerun the measurement below
# and replace the number. There is no automatic ratchet-up here (unlike
# gauntlet's scripts/coverage-floor.py) -- raising is a deliberate,
# reviewed edit, same as lowering would have to be.
#
# How these numbers were measured (orbit-launcher issue #169, 2026-10-05;
# two runs, identical to four decimal places):
#   scripts/coverage.sh -race    # unit tests plus the binary's pty runs
#   go run ./tools/coveragefloor coverage.out   # prints got% per package
# Measure where the gate runs: CI's `fast` job runs as root, so the three
# internal/deploy tests that force a permission error skip themselves
# there, and that package reads 94.2% in CI against 96.7% as a normal
# user. Its floor is the CI figure; every other package reads the same in
# both places.
#
# Each floor below is the measured percentage rounded DOWN to one decimal
# place -- never up, so the recorded floor is never stricter than what was
# actually observed.
#
# Only packages that have test files appear here. A package with no tests
# still shows up in the coverage profile at 0%, but adding its floor is a
# deliberate choice made here, not something tools/coveragefloor enforces
# on its own (see that command's package doc). Packages under test/ are
# black-box/integration packages, not the module's own package tree, and
# are intentionally out of scope for this file -- except
# test/internal/vtscreen, the screen reader the pty and live suites stand
# on, which has unit tests of its own.

github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/cmd/orbit-launcher 94.1
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/deploy 94.2
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/engine 93.4
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/release 100.0
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/ui 98.2
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/ui/starfield 90.2
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/internal/ui/style 100.0
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/calculateversion 96.5
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/coveragefloor 97.3
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/coveragefloor/floor 94.5
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/licencenotices 95.5
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/licencenotices/notices 96.4
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/licencereview 97.3
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/licencereview/review 99.3
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/supplychainpolicy 98.3
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/tools/supplychainpolicy/policy 99.2
github.com/tomlawesome/orbit-launcher/test/internal/vtscreen 93.5
